findings.where: Nav bar (the binding strip), the logo at top left, at desktop and phone
findings.fault: The logo has been recoloured. The arches and 'MMM INFRA' are a pale cream-yellow on the binding red, not the logo's grey arches and blue wordmark, and 'Moseley Infrastructure Advisory Services' is gone. Neither the logo blue nor the logo grey appears anywhere in the palette, either as a colour with a job or marked as logo-only. So the page drops the client's own colours without saying so.
findings.who_objects: Mark, whose logo stays as it is (client value 7, brand sheet §4). The house rule says a reversed version is made only with the client's yes. A visitor who knows MMM Infra from its current site or LinkedIn also sees a different mark here.

findings.where: Hero, the 'Write to me' note in the left margin (desktop); below the italic line (phone)
findings.fault: The page's one action is the lightest thing in the hero. On desktop it is a small, tilted red scribble about 130 px wide, out in the gutter left of the margin line and away from the text column. The heading, the clipped photo and the large aqueduct drawing all come before it. It reads as a note on the pad, not as the way to get in touch.
findings.who_objects: The development-bank official who has decided Mark is worth a word. They look for how to reach him under the introduction and find nothing there. They either fall back on the nav's 'Contact' or miss the route.

findings.where: Whole page: no footer, and nowhere the email address is shown
findings.fault: The page ends on the motion-sketch box with no footer, even though the palette names the binding colour for 'nav, footer'. The email address never appears as readable text. 'Write to me' only opens a mail program, so a visitor who uses webmail, or who wants to copy the address into a procurement shortlist, gets nothing to copy.
findings.who_objects: The bank official, who often forwards an advisor's contact details to colleagues or files them, and needs the address itself rather than a mail program opening (first-visit trust item 7).

findings.where: Article specimen headline 'The World's Best Public- / Private Partnership Law' and the handwritten pull quote (desktop); the pull quote again at phone, across four lines
findings.fault: Every line is snapped to the 32 px rules, so a two-line heading gets a full empty rule between its lines. The headline reads as two separate headings, with 'Public-' hanging at a line end. The script quote spreads over two lines on desktop and four on phone with large gaps between them. The small captions in the palette, texture and type-pair notes read as double-spaced lists, not as sentences.
findings.who_objects: Any reader of an article page, which this specimen sets the look for (mode Read). A heading that falls apart into two lines slows the scan. Angélique's longer post titles will break this way on every post.

findings.where: Article specimen, the 'Streamlining the PPP Process…' lecture row
findings.fault: The row's bottom rule runs right along the baseline of 'Lecture · 23 April 2026 · PDF', so the date and the PDF label look underlined as well. The title's own link underline merges into that rule. A reader cannot tell whether the title, the 'PDF' label or the whole row is the link.
findings.who_objects: A visitor looking for Mark's talks and papers, which is the proof an official looks for (first-visit trust item 4). They hesitate over where to click on the one row that shows his work.

findings.where: The style tile as a whole (palette to motion sketch)
findings.fault: The brief asks each tile for a button, but this tile has none. The only actions are the script margin note and 'Replay the note', which is a button styled as an underlined link. That gives the layout round no button style, and 'Replay' takes the link's underline even though it acts in place.
findings.who_objects: The layout-round designer and Angélique. Both will need an ordinary button (for example 'Download CV' or a form's send) and have none to draw from. A visitor gets a link-looking control that stays on the page.

findings.where: Hero, the italic line 'Over 40 years of international infrastructure experience.' and the first screen as a whole
findings.fault: Next to his name, the hero offers a length-of-service phrase as its proof. Nothing in view says which regions or kinds of work. The visitor gets one checkable fact (the World Bank PPP Group) and an adjective-style claim, with no place or region of work.
findings.who_objects: The bank official, who shortlists advisors on relevant projects and regions. 'Over 40 years' is the kind of size claim they discount, and missing regions leaves them unsure he covers theirs (first-visit trust items 3 and 6, 'Feel the CV').

findings.where: Ground: the double margin line and the ruled feints across the page
findings.fault: On the page, the double margin line renders as a thin dark brown-olive line, not the 'margin red' the palette names. The feints read greyish rather than the pale blue shown in the texture swatch. These two cues are what make the yellow read as a legal pad and not a plain yellow page, and both come out muddy.
findings.who_objects: Mark, who chose the legal pad 'given my legal background'. If the pad's signature red margin does not read, the page loses the lawyer's-paper meaning he asked for and is left with a strong yellow.

findings.where: Motion sketch timeline table, at phone
findings.fault: The four-column table squeezes the 'Element' column to about 95 px, so the hold row's description runs down ten one- and two-word lines.
findings.who_objects: Anyone reviewing the tile on a phone, including Mark answering the questionnaire. The table becomes a narrow strip that is slow to read.
